growthNote: Almost all of the 2025 growth is upstream: the new length sits in Bengaluru North and Yelahanka, with Bangalore-South roughly doubling. The central (Ramanagara, Magadi) and southern (Kanakapura) reaches were already mapped as polluted in 2018.
priorityNote: Priority is CPCB's BOD-based class (V in 2011, III in 2018). On the same 2022-23 data the boards diverge: CPCB reads Priority I, but KSPCB's own lab analysis reads Priority IV - and KSPCB's April-2026 dossier cover letter to NMCG (19 June 2026) presses the point, arguing Karnataka has 6 polluted stretches, not CPCB's 14. The August-2025 NMCG report still listed III, predating the October reclassification. Lengths shown are Paani Earth's mapping (CPCB did not specify a length).
mprOverview: Tracked under NGT order OA 673/2018 through monthly NMCG progress reports (2020-2026), which itemise the two stretch ULBs - Ramanagara and Kanakapura - and the V-Valley catchment as the upstream source.
reportingCaveat: Figures here are what the official documents (NMCG MPRs, District Environment Plans) report. Where something shows as nil, not submitted, or unmentioned, it means it is not recorded in those documents - it may still be present or happening on the ground, or held in non-public records.
levelCoverage: Sewage and solid waste are reported at ULB (town) level - yearly for Ramanagara and Kanakapura, a single DEP snapshot for Magadi, Harohalli and Bidadi. Hazardous and biomedical waste are reported at district level (Bengaluru Urban, Ramanagara); industrial effluent at the V-Valley catchment. No Gram-Panchayat-level data appears in the reports we have reviewed, and rural taluk areas outside the towns are not separately reported.
bodCaveat: Why Priority I: CPCB classifies purely by BOD bands - Priority I is a worst monitoring point above 30 mg/L (Priority III is 10-20). The Arkavathi reads 72 mg/L at Hesaraghatta, placing it in Priority I - up from the 10-20 band (III) in 2018. Priority uses BOD alone, from grab samples: a high value can mean more organic pollution OR less dilution in low-flow months, so it needs flow context, and it misses heavy metals that independent studies have documented here.

evidence.headline: Pollution here is documented consistently over years - and well beyond the single BOD number.
points: CPCB Oct-2025 monitoring: max BOD 72 mg/L at Hesaraghatta, 46 d/s Kanakapura, 21 Tippagondanahalli, 11 Manchanabale.
NWMP monitoring (Mar 2024-May 2025): BOD up to 30 mg/L at Thippagondanahalli and 52 mg/L d/s Kanakapura; dissolved oxygen frequently below 4 mg/L.
ATREE: heavy metals found in milk, fodder and vegetables in villages along the Vrishabhavathi.
Arkavathi Horata Samithi and Paani Earth: RTI-sourced lab analyses.

Paani Earth x ICCW (IIT Madras), Feb-Mar 2024: 7 sites on the Arkavathi and Vrishabhavathi tested for 65 water + 20 sediment parameters. Banned pesticides (heptachlor, DDT) up to ~25,000x US-EPA guidelines, PAHs up to ~3,000x, mercury in sediment up to 26x Canadian guidelines, and phosphorus at eutrophic levels at every site - contamination the BOD-only official classification does not capture.

link.label: Read the full report: Uncovering Hidden Pollution in the Arkavathi (Paani Earth x ICCW)

tabs.label: Industrial effluent
tabs.source: NMCG MPRs; District Environmental Plans (2021, 2022); CAG Report No. 8 of 2017; Neer Vazhvu spatial estimates
tabs.intro: Government reports state that no industrial effluent reaches the river. Below is what each public record reports.
tabs.summaryLine: Full treatment reported; CETP coverage limited (CAG); 144 to 191 industries

categories.label: Discharges
categories.body: Government reports ~4.7 MLD of trade effluent (V-Valley), fully treated with zero discharge to the river. What each record shows:
points: Trade effluent (V-Valley): ~4.7 MLD, reported treated in 33 ETPs - ~3.3 MLD recycled, ~1.4 MLD used on land, ~0.02 MLD sent to common ETPs; reported as not discharged to the river (NMCG 2025).
Sewage from these industries (V-Valley): ~3.3 MLD - ~1.1 MLD recycled, ~2.1 MLD used on land (NMCG 2025).
Industries (V-Valley catchment): grew 144 (2020) to 191 (2025); 14 units connected to a common ETP, unchanged 2022-2025.
F-register (basin): ~5.65 MLD of trade effluent from 562 units, reported fully treated / recycled (2021); BBMP's Vrishabhavathi valley alone reports 25.34 MLD (DEP 2022).
CAG audit (2017): 38 of 66 sampled KIADB areas had no CETP - worth reconciling with the full-treatment claim.

categories.label: Industrial areas
categories.body: Common effluent treatment plant (CETP) coverage of the industrial areas along the stretch:
points: No CETP reported in Ramanagara district (DEP 2021).
Harohalli KIADB (1st-4th phases): nearest common ETP >20 km (Neer Vazhvu estimate).
Across the basin ~26 of 56 industrial areas have no CETP within ~5 km (8 of 18 KIADB).

categories.label: Contaminated clusters
categories.body: Officially recognised pollution hotspots in the catchment:
points: Peenya (Vrishabhavathi valley): CPCB Critically Polluted Area (CEPI 78.12); NGT OA 1038/2018. Among CPCB's five confirmed contaminated sites in Bengaluru.
Mavallipura dumpsite (Yelahanka): manganese in groundwater; also among CPCB's five confirmed contaminated sites.
Status: KSPCB sought to delist the sites; CPCB directed fresh soil / water / sediment sampling and a State-Level Empowered Monitoring Committee - a remediation plan is still awaited.
Hazardous waste: no TSDF or SLF reported in Bengaluru Urban; 1,718 HW-generating industries (DEP 2022).

categories.label: Draining into the stretch
categories.body: Two industrial areas sit within a few hundred metres of the stretch (near Acchalu Village, Ramanagara taluk); the MPRs name two Red-category units there and report their effluent as treated and recycled. The larger clusters - Peenya, Bidadi, Harohalli, Doddaballapura - lie roughly 6-10 km upstream in the Vrishabhavathi valley and reach the stretch through the valley's drain network, consistent with the MPRs' own note that the Arkavathi's pollution originates mainly upstream in the V-Valley catchment. Open the Pressures floor for the industrial areas and their CETP coverage.

categories.label: Registered industries (KSPCB F-register)
categories.body: The basin's KSPCB Regional Offices list ~11,800 consented industries (F-register, as on 31-03-2019) - at least ~37% in the Red or Orange (higher-pollution) categories. The Vrishabhavathi valley alone (Peenya + Dasarahalli) accounts for ~7,000. Per-taluk counts sit on the Gaps layer. Figures are approximate - OCR-extracted from scanned 2019 registers:
points: Ramanagara district (~1,357): Ramanagara ~650, Kanakapura ~510, Magadi ~120, Channapatna ~80.
Bengaluru / Vrishabhavathi valley: Peenya ~5,070, Dasarahalli ~1,960 - the basin's industrial core.
Arkavathi headwaters: Nelamangala ~1,950, Doddaballapura ~1,450.
~4,400 Red/Orange industries basin-wide, against only ~12 on CPCB continuous monitoring (below) - the accountability gap in one line.

categories.label: Continuous monitoring (OCEMS)
categories.body: Twelve industries in the Arkavathi catchment are enrolled in CPCB's OCEMS real-time online effluent/emission monitoring - seven monitoring liquid effluent (flow / pH / TDS at the outlet), the rest monitoring stack emissions. But every parameter reads "NA" in CPCB's public feed, and the live connectivity dashboard (who is transmitting vs offline) is captcha-gated - so none of these self-reported readings are publicly verifiable. What the public record shows (CPCB OCEMS: cems.cpcb.gov.in, rtdms.cpcb.gov.in; accessed July 2026):
points: Effluent-monitored (7, pharma): Anthem Biosciences (Ramanagara), Eurofins Advinus BioPharma (Ramanagara), Neoanthem Lifesciences (Harohalli), Gomti Research & Pharmachem (Kumbalgodu), Bio-gen Extracts (Dobaspet), Racs Pharma Chem and R L Fine Chem (Kudumalakunte).

Emission/stack-monitored (5): KPC Gas Power (Bidadi, power), Mukand Sumi Special Steel (Kanakapura), E Nano Incintech (Kanakapura) and Ramky Enviro (Doddaballapura) - common hazardous-waste incinerators, Maridi Bio (Harohalli, biomedical incinerator).
Every one of these industries' parameter values is "NA" in the public OCEMS feed; live values and connectivity status sit behind a login / captcha wall.

Coverage is partial by design: only large "17-category" industries are on OCEMS, and Bengaluru-urban units cannot be assigned to the Arkavathi sub-basin from public city labels (the feed carries no coordinates).

tabs.label: Treated-water reuse
tabs.summaryLine: Reuse is mandated (GoK 2016/2024); MPRs report partial reuse; the treated-water sale scheme never took off

categories.label: Reported reuse (MPR)
categories.body: Reuse of treated water as reported in the NMCG August-2025 MPR:
points: Treated water is used on-land for gardening / irrigation, recycled for process, and toilet flushing.
V-Valley: ~1.08 MLD treated sewage and ~3.32 MLD treated trade effluent recycled; ~2.06 + ~1.36 MLD discharged on-land for gardening.
On the ground: after BWSSB's buy-back arrangement dried up, Bengaluru apartments report letting treated water flow into drains - the reuse market has not taken off (Times of India).

link.label: TOI: apartments let treated water flow into drains

categories.label: STP mandate (GoK)
categories.body: Who must install an STP and reuse treated water - GoK notification FEE 316 EPC 2015 (19.01.2016), as amended by corrigendum FEE 43 EPC 2022 (12.03.2024):
points: Sewered areas: residential group housing / apartments with 120 units or more (or generating 80 KLD sewage); commercial buildings of 5,000 sqm or 35 KLD; educational institutions of 5,000 sqm; townships of 10 acres and above.
Unsewered areas: the thresholds tighten to 20 units or more / 2,000 sqm built-up for apartments and 2,000 sqm for commercial buildings.
Non-compliance draws an additional levy of 25-50% (residential) or 50-100% (non-residential) of water and sanitary charges until the STP is established (BWSSB circular, 14.03.2024).

categories.label: Sale of treated water
categories.body: In March 2024 BWSSB allowed apartments to sell up to 50% of the treated water from their in-situ STPs (reported during the 2024 water crisis).
points: The order itself is not in the public record - Paani Earth has filed an RTI for a copy (July 2026).

link.label: The Hindu: apartments can sell 50% of treated water

categories.label: OCEMS for private STPs
categories.body: KSPCB memo PCB/150/Infra/2025 (9 Oct 2025) mandates online continuous effluent monitoring (OCEMS) at private STPs above 500 KLD - residential apartments, commercial buildings and other organisations - as the first stage, with regional officers directed to list qualifying STPs within 7 days.
points: Memo obtained by Paani Earth via RTI (July 2026); earlier industry media had reported the threshold as 100 KLD. Coverage and compliance data are still not published.

tabs.label: Flood plain
tabs.source: KSPCB Action Plan (Sept 2019) + NMCG MPR August-2025
tabs.intro: The action plan's Flood Plain Zone section (item IV) makes four commitments, every one with the same deadline: 'within six months' - that is, by around March 2020. The September 2025 MPR, the last stretch-wise edition, is the yardstick below.
tabs.summaryLine: FPZ still un-notified and encroachment details still being gathered, six years past the plan's six-month deadline; plantation has a submitted plan, not reported work

categories.label: FPZ notification
categories.body: Action plan IV(d): notification of the Flood Plain Zone - State Government / Water Resources Department, within six months.
points: MPR August-2025 (item XVII, demarcation of floodplain and removal of illegal encroachments): tahsildars of the concerned taluks 'are in the process of obtaining the details on encroachment of lands of flood plain and upon receipt of the same they would initiate further needful action.'
Six years past the deadline, the zone that was to be notified by March 2020 is still at the details-gathering stage; no notification is reported in any MPR edition we hold.

categories.label: Encroachment check
categories.body: Action plan IV(b): checking encroachments in the FPZ of the river Arkavathi - District and Local administration / DMA, within six months.
points: Same MPR item XVII applies: encroachment details are being compiled by tahsildars; removal ('further needful action') is contingent on those details arriving.
The MPR language has stayed at this process stage across editions - no count of encroachments identified or removed has ever been reported for the stretch.

categories.label: Plantation & biodiversity park
categories.body: Action plan IV(a): plantation in the Flood Plain Zone - Karnataka State Forest Department, within six months.
points: MPR August-2025 (item XIX): the Forest Department has submitted an action plan for plantation of saplings and creation of an eco park on the Arkavathi stretch, with Rs 13.49 crore earmarked and completion 'within time frame of March 2024' per its letter - a deadline already 17 months past at the reporting date, for a plan still described as submitted, not executed.
Item XX (development of biodiversity park) is blank for this stretch in the same edition.
No extent, location or survival figures exist anywhere in the record, so nothing can yet be quantified against the action plan's commitment.

categories.label: Plastic & biomedical waste in drains
categories.body: Action plan IV(c): prohibition of disposal of municipal plastic and biomedical waste, particularly in drains - Local administration / DMA, within six months.
points: No MPR item corresponds to this commitment in the editions we hold - enforcement of the prohibition is unreported.
Biomedical waste is otherwise absent from stretch reporting entirely - the same systemic gap found in every action plan on this atlas.

keyTerms.note: A river stretch where BOD exceeds 3 mg/L, the Primary Water Quality Criteria for Bathing Water (organised outdoor bathing). CPCB identifies these stretches and prioritises them for restoration.
Oxygen consumed by microbes breaking down organic matter in the water; CPCB's core pollution indicator. Above 3 mg/L a location is considered polluted.
Based on the worst BOD reading in the stretch: Priority I above 30 mg/L (most polluted), II 20-30, III 10-20, IV 6-10, V 3-6. The Arkavathi reads up to 72 mg/L.
The national pollution regulator; publishes the polluted-river-stretch assessments (2018, October 2025).
The state regulator; runs the monitoring network and reports restoration progress for Karnataka's stretches.
Submitted by KSPCB / state agencies to NMCG as per the NGT orders (OA 673/2018), reporting action-plan implementation for each polluted stretch.
The environmental court whose orders drive the restoration programme, the action plans and the monthly reporting.
Hosts the national reporting and grievance infrastructure used for polluted river stretches across India.
A town or city municipal body (e.g. Ramanagara, Kanakapura) responsible for sewage and solid waste within its limits.
STPs treat sewered wastewater; FSTPs treat septage collected from septic tanks in unsewered areas.
A shared treatment plant for clusters of industries too small to run their own effluent treatment.
Real-time effluent sensors that industries and large private STPs are required to install and connect to the boards.

No. 593/2017 (Paryavaran Suraksha Samiti), the NGT directed CPCB to prepare a 'river basin-wise macro picture' identifying gaps and required interventions for ETPs, CETPs, STPs, Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) facilities and legacy waste sites.
